newsitem.title: USA: DLJ Q1 operating earnings up 33 percent.
newsitem.headline: DLJ Q1 operating earnings up 33 percent.

text.p: Equitable Cos Inc said its Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette affiliate's first quarter after-tax operating earnings rose 33 percent to $86.4 million compared with $65.1 million a year ago.

"This record first quarter performance resulted from strong merger and acquisition and underwriting activities during the first three months of the year," Equitable chief executive Joseph Melone said.
"Also contributing to the quarter's growth were higher profits from fixed income trading and from DLJ's Pershing Division," he said.
"Our principal investment businesses -- Alliance Capital and DLJ -- continued to turn in record performances," Melone said.
"While both companies have benefited from the positive capital market environment, their growth and success has exceeded those of most of their peers."
The aggregate after-tax operating earnings contribution from Equitable's investment companies totaled $76.5 million for the quarter, up 29 percent from a year ago.
The 1996 amount excludes an $11.0 million after-tax gain from the sale of Alliance units.
Total assets under management by the company and its subsidiaries increased to $240.8 billion, up 14 percent.
For the first quarter, Alliance's after-tax operating earnings -- before minority interests and other expenses -- rose 18 percent to $53.3 million compared with $45.1 million a year ago.
